Minbox text archive

Your messages, organized for useful answers.

minbox-text-archive helps you collect your text conversations, filter authentication codes and clear spam, and keep a private archive in your own Google Drive.

minbox-text-archive is the Minbox text archive software. It runs on your own always-on collection computer. Your archive is separate from this public information site.

How it works

  1. You authorize collection from your own messaging account. Android uses Google Messages on Linux; the iPhone adapter uses Messages on your own Mac. Android collection on Mac or Windows is not implemented.
  2. Your collection computer keeps available messages and source identifiers in a local archive, filters excluded content, and updates private Google Docs in your Drive.
  3. You connect your Drive to a compatible AI service yourself to ask questions and follow citations to original messages. That service has separate permissions. An optional check can confirm that it retrieves a familiar message with the correct date and source link; skipping the check does not block collection or publication. Connector availability depends on your account and provider.

Your account, your archive

You create a private folder with any name, then select it while signing in to Google. Minbox requests Google’s drive.file permission for selected and app-created files. This is per-file access, not a recursive folder grant; Minbox separately checks the signed-in owner, private root and managed parent bindings. Unrelated files you add to the folder are not automatically authorized or imported. Renaming your folder keeps the connection working. Archive documents retain owner-based names, such as “Casey Text Archive” (a fictional example). Archived messages are not published on this site.

Corrections and limits

A designated Corrections document records explicit changes, such as marking a message as spam. Personal labels keep a message in the full private archive while excluding it from narrower work views.

Collection is limited to accessible history. Available original images are verified, stored privately and linked to their messages. Optional local OCR is labeled as machine-extracted text and can contain errors. Unavailable or unsupported attachments remain explicit gaps. AI answers can be mistaken, and an archive is not proof of complete phone coverage.

Android/Linux phone-to-Drive capture and images have been verified in an existing installation; independent client installation still needs acceptance. The Mac/iPhone adapter is fixture-tested; live synchronization, permissions and background operation still need verification on the owner’s machine.

Health and notifications

Reviewed local recovery handles ordinary failures. Only unresolved emergencies requiring human action are eligible for email; routine failures, reminders and recovery do not send mail. External delivery is optional and separately configured with the owner. A local monitor cannot notify during complete host or network failure.
